title: Sequence-level layer: which fin-size genes are present in the annotated flying-fish gene set, and what the lat4a convergent site does and does not show
layer_boundary: THIS IS A SEQUENCE LAYER AND NOTHING MORE. An orthologue call shows a gene is present in a flying fish. Every other link in this project's map rests on expression or phenotype, which do not exist for any flying fish. Presence is not place of action and not time of action, so a sequence result must never be combined with a phenotype grade into one confidence, and a gene's chain strength is unchanged by having been found in the gene set.

source.owner: the sequences thread (sequences/genes.json, gliders.json, progression.json); this thread only reads them
source.flying_fish_gene_set: Annotated Hirundichthys speculiger proteins exist (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700; figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1, pep.fa, 13 MB) for the same assembly as GCA_018398805.1 (which NCBI holds unannotated). Orthologues were called by reciprocal best blastp hit to the zebrafish proteome; where that fails (kcnh2a, shha) the alignment uses tblastn hits on the assembly, labelled. Medaka (Beloniformes) remains in every alignment as the closest Ensembl-annotated relative. H. speculiger is not one of the species measured for fin length by Daane 2021, so it is cross-species within the family.
source.method: reciprocal best hit against the zebrafish proteome
source.birds_excluded: Birds (class Aves) are this project's frozen holdout and are excluded until the holdout exam runs.

orthologues_resolved.what_this_adds: The gene is present in the annotated flying-fish gene set as a clean reciprocal best hit, so the proxy-species work on it is about a gene the flying fish actually has. It adds nothing about expression, stage or function in a flying fish.

orthologues_not_resolved.what_this_adds: A sequence similar to this gene exists in the flying fish, but which paralogue it is was not resolved.
orthologues_not_resolved.why_not_an_orthologue_call: Reciprocal best hit FAILED: the flying-fish protein's best match back in the zebrafish proteome is kcnh7a, not kcnh2a. This is a hit found by searching a zebrafish or medaka protein against the flying-fish set, not an orthologue call, and it must not be reported as one. For a duplicated gene family this is the expected failure mode and it means the paralogue cannot be distinguished at this identity level.

lat4a_convergent_site.site: lat4a (ZFIN slc43a2a) position 326, the F326L substitution Daane 2021 reports as convergent in gliding beloniforms
lat4a_convergent_site.it_tracks_gliding_within_beloniformes: The derived L is carried by the annotated flying-fish protein, by 8 of 9 flying fishes in Daane's exon data (Parexocoetus is F, as the paper itself says) and by BOTH gliding halfbeak genera, while the non-gliding relatives carry the ancestral F with one saury carrying I. So within this order the substitution does track gliding.

there_is_no_convergence_with_gliding_MAM.finding: Outside Beloniformes the site is ancestral in every glider tested: all three bats, both colugos, the sugar glider, plus mouse, human, the reptile controls and the frog all carry F. So this is a beloniform-specific change, NOT a general gliding signature, and it must not be presented as convergence with gliding mammals.
there_is_no_convergence_with_gliding_MAM.caveat_from_the_sequences_thread: The nine genes were chosen from zebrafish fin biology, not from glider biology, so absence of convergence here says nothing about the rest of the genome.

three_reasons_this_is_weaker_than_it_loo: THE LADDER IS FLAT, AND SLIGHTLY INVERTED. Gliding halfbeaks carry a mean of 24 derived states of the 38 sites at a fin ratio of 0.274, while flying fishes carry 21.4 at a fin ratio of 0.687. The count therefore does not scale with fin length, and the group with the smaller fin carries marginally MORE derived residues. Nothing here is a dose-response.

THE NON-GLIDER ZERO IS CIRCULAR. Daane's sheet G lists only substitutions shared by gliders and absent from outgroups, so non-gliding species score zero at these sites by construction. The zero is a property of how the site list was built, not a finding about non-gliders.

TRACKING IS NOT CAUSING, and this project's own phenotype layer agrees: the chain for slc43a2a has a weakest link graded hypothesis, because nothing experimental connects the transporter's function to fin ray length in any species. A sequence that tracks a trait does not supply that missing step.
lat4a_convergent_site.statistics_note: A LADDER TO READ, NOT A TEST. Four groups (needlefish/saury, halfbeak, gliding halfbeak, flying fish) is far too few for any statistical claim. No correlation between residue state and fin ratio is computed: species share ancestry, so a cross-species correlation needs phylogenetic correction, and with four groups that correction cannot be done meaningfully.

what_this_layer_changes_about_the_fin_si: It removes one objection: the fin-size genes are not absent from flying fish. Seven of nine are present as clean reciprocal best hits, with 56 to 89 percent identity to their zebrafish counterparts.
It strengthens the lat4a identification by one more independent route: the annotated flying-fish protein carries the derived residue that Daane's exon data report.
It does NOT raise any gene's evidence grade, because no grade in this project rests on presence.
It does NOT make the flying fish a model organism: there is still no expression, no mutant and no functional measurement in any flying fish.
kcnh2a and shha are the two genes it cannot speak for, and they include one of the three wing genes.
species_caveat: The annotated gene set is Hirundichthys speculiger. The fin measurements this project uses are Cheilopogon furcatus, Exocoetus volitans and Hirundichthys rondeleti. Only the last shares a genus with the sequenced animal, so sequence and morphometry are cross-species within Exocoetidae wherever they are used together.
